steps.prompt_exact: I'm planning Instagram carousels on my phone; build me a small offline browser checker where I can enter a topic and slide ideas, reorder them, see hook strength, continuity gaps, CTA fit, and copy a compact slide brief.
steps.response_exact:
Claude responded: Now let me plan the design before building:
Reading frontend design skill
Reading frontend design skill

Now let me plan the design before building:

Brief: Mobile-first carousel planner for Instagram. Subject: social content strategy. Audience: creators/marketers building on phone. Single job: evaluate slide deck structure before publishing.

Design plan:

Palette: near-black 
#0F0F0F bg, 
#F0F0F0 text, 
#FF5C5C accent (hook/alert), 
#A8FF78 success green (good CTA/continuity), #888 muted. Avoids the acid-green-on-black cliché by pairing coral-red with the green.
Type: Inter (utility/body, tight tracking for mobile), Syne (display face for section labels — angular, editorial without being editorial-cliché)
Signature: Slide cards that visually pulse/dim based on hook strength — the card itself becomes the diagnostic feedback, not just a badge.
Layout: Single-column, full-width on mobile. Cards stack vertically with drag handles. Sticky analysis bar at bottom.
Created a file, read a file
Created a file, read a file

Here's what you've got — all offline, single file, no dependencies.

How it works:

Each slide card has three fields (Headline, Body, CTA/Transition line) and a role tag (Hook / Value / Bridge / CTA). As you type:

The colored top bar on each card updates live to show hook strength — green = strong, yellow = passable, red = weak
Hook score (0–5) is heuristic: questions, numbers, power words ("Why", "Stop", "Secret", etc.), short punchy length all push it up
Flow % looks at keyword overlap between adjacent slides and flags sudden topic jumps
CTA % checks whether your last slide is tagged CTA, has an action verb (follow, save, share, dm…), and warns if you've got multiple CTAs competing

The fixed bottom bar shows all three scores at a glance with fill bars, plus an alerts feed. "Copy Brief" dumps a compact plain-text summary you can paste into Notes or a DM.

To reorder: drag cards on desktop, or swipe a card up/down past a ~56px threshold on mobile (it snaps to the new position).

steps.prompt_exact: This is close, but it uses Google Fonts and builds the slide and alert UI with innerHTML, so pasted slide text could be treated as HTML. Please return the complete single-file HTML again using only system fonts and safe DOM creation with textContent/addEventListener, keeping the same carousel checker features.
steps.response_exact:
Claude responded: Good.
Read the current file to work from
Read the current file to work from

Good. I have the full source. Now I'll rewrite it cleanly — stripping the Google Fonts import, swapping font stacks to system fonts, and replacing every innerHTML assignment that touches user/slide data or alert messages with safe DOM construction via createElement + textContent.

Ran 2 commands
Ran 2 commands

Both innerHTML hits are comments, not assignments. Clean on both counts.

Presented file
Presented file

Both issues are fully resolved:

Google Fonts → gone. The font stack is now 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif for display elements and system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif for body — no network request at all, works fully offline.

innerHTML → gone everywhere that touches data. The whole render pipeline now uses a small el() helper that calls createElement and sets content with .textContent or .value. That covers slide cards (headline, body, CTA fields, role selects, hook dots), alert items, the empty state, and the static header text. The only two innerHTML occurrences left in the file are comments describing what was removed.

Everything else — hook scoring, flow/CTA analysis, drag-to-reorder, touch reorder, copy brief — is unchanged.
